<a id="keeping-pace-under-a-bounded-census--有界普查之下的同步"></a>
# Keeping pace under a bounded census

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`bounded-census-keeps-pace` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](bounded-census-keeps-pace.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where the list returns within some number at arbitrarily late steps, coming to be and ceasing to be keep pace; under a bound growing without end, however slowly, arising can go on without ceasing.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Where the members of which a determination holds are listed at each step, each once, from some step T on at most B at each step, and the determination is decided at each step, members coming to hold at arbitrarily late steps need members ceasing to hold at arbitrarily late steps. (`Becoming.Listed`, `Becoming.Listed.ceasing_of_coming`)
2. The proof goes through the census balance: with coming to be recurring, the comings from any step on accumulate past B; where the list returns within B, the list at the end is shorter than the list at the start with what came between, so by the balance something ceases between. (`Becoming.recurring_accumulates`, `Becoming.Listed.ceasing_iff_shortfall`)
3. So the bound need not hold at every step from some step on: the list need only return within some number K at arbitrarily late steps. (`Becoming.Listed.ceasing_of_returning`)
4. With the census law (ceasing-needs-arising), the two recur together where the list is bounded from some step on: coming to be recurs exactly when ceasing to be does. (`Becoming.Listed.coming_iff_ceasing`)
5. Read of activity: under a census with at most B formations active at each step from some step on, arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs. (`Becoming.Web.Census`, `Becoming.Web.ceasing_of_arising`, `Becoming.Web.unceasing_iff_bounded`)
6. Read of worlds: in a world whose relata active at each step are listed, at most B of them, arising recurs exactly when ceasing does. (`Becoming.World.CountedWithin`, `Becoming.World.CountedWithin.arising_iff_ceasing`)
7. Every census of a finite world is bounded, with no decidability, and where activity is decided one exists, the premise of the bounded law; the law of finite worlds is World.arising_iff_ceasing of Becoming.Space. (`Becoming.World.Finite`, `Becoming.World.Finite.census_bounded`, `Becoming.World.Finite.countedWithin`, `Becoming.World.arising_iff_ceasing`)
8. In procession, where relatum x is active at step x alone, one relatum is active at each step and arising and ceasing both recur, while the relata are not finitely many, so the law reaches beyond finite worlds; accretion has a census without a bound, and arising recurs there while ceasing does not. (`Becoming.World.procession`, `Becoming.World.procession_world`, `Becoming.World.accretion`, `Becoming.World.accretion_unbounded`)
9. The bound may vary with the steps: where at most B t relata are active at each step t, listed (a constant bound being the case), and B returns within some number at arbitrarily late steps, arising recurs exactly when ceasing does. (`Becoming.World.CountedBy`, `Becoming.World.CountedBy.arising_iff_ceasing`)
10. A bound growing without end, however slowly, does not keep the two together: for any non-decreasing, unbounded B, in slow B the relata below B t are active at step t, with a census counted by B; relatum B t arises across each step at which B grows, and nothing ceases; so under logarithmic growth, for instance, arising can still go on without ceasing. (`Becoming.World.slow`, `Becoming.World.slow_world`)
11. Where the list grows without end, ceasing to be recurs where, from each step, the comings over some stretch outnumber the bound at its end; this is sufficient, not necessary, and in slow the comings never outnumber the bound; the exact criterion is the shortfall of census-balance. (`Becoming.Listed.ceasing_of_outpacing`, `Becoming.Listed.ceasing_iff_shortfall`)
12. Read of standing: where from some step on at most B conditions stand at each step, listed, coming to stand recurs exactly when ceasing to stand does. Read of dependence: where the dependences of each step are listed, at most B from some step on, forming recurs exactly when dissolving does. (`Becoming.Web.StandingCensus`, `Becoming.Web.StandingCensus.coming_iff_ceasing`, `Becoming.Web.DependenceCensus`, `Becoming.Web.DependenceCensus.forming_iff_dissolving`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- A listing bounded from some step on: the members holding at each step are listed, each once, with every list from some step T on no longer than one bound B; there may be infinitely many members in all.
- The world premise CountedWithin asks the bound at every step, the case T = 0. The more general form asks only that the list return within some number K at arbitrarily late steps (ceasing_of_returning, CountedBy.arising_iff_ceasing).
- Decidability: read of activity this is decided activity, read of standing it holds automatically; it is a logical commitment of the representation and classically always holds.
- procession_world, accretion_unbounded and Finite.countedWithin are statements about particular worlds or about finite worlds; Finite.countedWithin needs decided activity to build a census; Finite.census_bounded does not.
- slow_world asks the bound to be non-decreasing and unbounded and is a statement about one particular world; ceasing_of_outpacing asks every list to be no longer than the bound and, from each step, the comings over some stretch to outnumber the bound at its end.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The bound must return within one number at arbitrarily late steps; the law fails where the bound grows without end, however slowly (accretion, slow). Witness: `Becoming.World.slow_world`.
- That a non-decreasing bound either stays within some number or grows without end is classical; the pure core states the two sides separately.
- For a bound that is not monotone and eventually exceeds every number no corresponding world is given (its construction needs data from existence).
- The law is a count, not a mechanism: it says neither which member comes to be or ceases nor that the two are causally linked.
- **Counterexample:** accretion: a census without a bound, arising recurring and ceasing not, so the bound is needed; procession: bounded but not finite, so finiteness is not needed. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Openness.lean)
- **Counterexample:** slow: for any non-decreasing, unbounded bound B, a census counted by B, arising recurring and nothing ever ceasing, so no bound growing without end, however slowly, keeps the two together. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Openness.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · Uses decidability of the named determinations, a logical commitment written as a hypothesis. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

The law of a finite family (coming-and-ceasing-keep-pace: coming_recurs_iff, Web.unceasing_iff) needs one fixed finite family holding every member; here only the list at each step needs a bound, and the members may be infinitely many in all. So what the law of finite worlds needs (space-and-its-parts: in a finite world whose activity is decided arising recurring and ceasing recurring are one part) is a bound on the count, not finiteness. With the census law, the relation of arising and ceasing falls into three tiers by counting: with the active at each step finite and returning within some number at arbitrarily late steps, the two recur together; finite at each step and eventually beyond every number, ceasing needs arising and not conversely, however slowly the count grows (accretion, slow); no longer finite at each step, ceasing can recur alone (attrition has no census). The author's reading (an AI argument): in an unfolding whose active members never exceed a bound, lasting arising and lasting ceasing are two sides of one lasting change, as in a finite world, without the members being finitely many in all; renewed generations can be endless while those present together are bounded; nor need the bound always hold: those present together need only keep returning within some number, and growing without end, however slowly, they need not keep pace. This is a reading of activity and standing, arising and ceasing being names Ren confirmed (2026-10-09-arising-ceasing-names); it is not the proposal's generative and degenerative (Ren wrote ‘generative和degenerate虽然都在一个becoming model上，但是他们不overlap吧’, a tag question presuming that they do not overlap, so this reading is not what is meant; they read as widening and narrowing what can form, DELEGATED-CHOICES D2).
